tasks.title: Building large organic parts is slow: the raptor (99 features) takes ~14 s native, the Triceratops (82) ~9 s (opening is instant from the cache)
tasks.notes: Profiled 2026-10-20 (raptor): OCCT booleans ~7.2 s; **volume checks in the boolean guard ~2.3 s** (body volume recomputed every step, tool volumes again on retry, raw and merged measured every time); **fuzzy retry of the 30-loft fuse ~1.7 s** (first attempt wasted, see KER-1); **measuring 2.3 s** on every build (the regression from 10.6 s since K2 measuring); tessellating 0.3 s. Next: cache volumes on shapes and skip the raw/merged compare when merging changed nothing; send the mesh before dimensions and skip measuring unchanged bodies; then consider fuzzy-first for runs that need it (only with raptor parity)

tasks.title: B-rep validity in the health check: the raptor builds watertight but its final body (`torso`) fails BRepCheck (coincident/overlapping lofts)
tasks.notes: Confirmed 2026-10-20. It also costs speed: in the 30-loft fuse, merging faces changes the volume, the unmerged result fails BRepCheck, so the whole fuse is rebuilt with fuzzy 1e-4. Next: check validity after each timeline step to find the overlapping lofts, then ShapeFix, a Claude rule, or accept. OCCT 7.9.3 sometimes returns wrong booleans without an error; requiring BRepCheck on every result made things worse (more failures, 6× slower)

Assign materials and colours to objects: pick a material (and a colour, defaulting to the material's) for the whole part, a body, a group or a picked object; the viewport draws each in its colour, and the Objects panel shows a swatch
tasks.notes: Asked for 2026-10-24. tasks.title: Filament needed, and weight by material: the main question is *how much filament does this print take*: the Part panel shows it in grams and metres of 1.75 mm filament for the chosen material (as printed: walls plus infill), per body and in total, and what share of a 1 kg spool that is. Beside it the solid weight (cast, machined, or 100% infill: metals, wood, resin) and the surface area
tasks.notes: Asked for 2026-10-24. The volume is already measured (`PartMesh::volume_mm3`, per body in `BodySummary`); add the surface area (`BRepGProp::SurfaceProperties`, as `measure.rs` does per face). Rust owns the material presets (g/cm³: PLA 1.24, PETG 1.27, ABS 1.04, ASA 1.07, TPU 1.21, PA 1.14, PC 1.20; aluminium 2.70, steel 7.85, stainless 8.00, brass 8.50, copper 8.96, titanium 4.43; resin 1.15, oak 0.75) and the estimate (printed ≈ area × wall thickness + the rest × infill; defaults 0.8 mm walls, 15% infill, both editable; length = grams ÷ density ÷ 0.02405 cm² (the 1.75 mm cross-section); supports, brim and purge aren't counted, so it says so; the slicer has the exact figure). Uses the materials assigned by PRN-8: each body's weight and the total (a part-wide pick works before PRN-8 lands). A custom density covers anything not listed. Measured, never read from feature parameters
